edge.title: DynMuon: sigmoid-scheduled spectral power p applied around NS polar
edge.summary: DynMuon replaces Muon's update with fast_spectral: the NS polar factor of the Frobenius-normalized momentum X is left-multiplied by a 2nd-order Taylor polynomial of (XXᵀ)^(p/2) and scaled by ‖u‖_F^p, a surrogate for UΣ^pVᵀ that equals plain Muon at p=0. p follows a decreasing sigmoid from ≈+0.12 at step 0 through 0 at step 128 to ≈−0.25 after ~600 steps, so for most of training the update mildly up-weights weak singular directions and grows as the momentum norm shrinks. The gradient is divided by the 524288 batch tokens and momentum becomes heavy-ball (m ← 0.95m + g, Nesterov 0.95m + g); vs #1, WD 0.01→0.025 with lr 0.02 kept, #6-style init, train_steps 3600→3200 (claimed 3175).

changes.label: fast_spectral power correction
changes.detail: X = u/‖u‖_F (wide orientation), Y = NS(X) in fp32; E = XXᵀ − I, C = I + δE + ½δ(δ−1)E² with δ = p/2; update = C·Y·‖u‖_F^p, then × max(1,m/n)^0.5 (returns Y alone when |p| < 1e-12).

changes.label: Sigmoid schedule for p
changes.detail: get_dynmuon_p: p_t = −0.25 + 0.5/(1 + exp((t/3200 − 0.04)/0.04)); set_hparams writes it into group['spectral_p'] every step (spectral_lam forced to 0 and unused).

changes.label: Mean-grad heavy-ball momentum
changes.detail: dynmuon_update divides grad by 8·64·1024, uses momentum.mul_(0.95).add_(g) and Nesterov u = 0.95·m + g; direction-equivalent to the lerp form but 20× larger, which matters through ‖u‖_F^p.

changes.label: Muon WD 0.01 → 0.025
changes.detail: DynMuon(lr=0.02, weight_decay=0.025, p=0.0, lam=0.0); decoupled WD applied as in Muon.

changes.label: #6-style init
changes.detail: Non-proj weights N(0, 0.33/fan_in), embed N(0,1), all biases 0, gains 1 (proj weights still zero), replacing #1's PyTorch-default init.

changes.label: train_steps 3600 → 3200, claim 3175
changes.detail: Uses #12's cadence (validate every 25 steps after 90%); 3175 is 25 steps before the LR reaches 0.

changes.label: Re-indent + seeded trials
changes.detail: Whole file re-indented to 3 spaces, num_trials=25 seeded from SEED (random/numpy/torch), unused Muon/muon_update and lam kept, per-step time print removed.

edge.parent_check: Inferred #1 (lr 0.02 matches #1), but a whitespace-insensitive comparison shows the skeleton is #6's (num_trials loop, normal init, zero biases, F.rms_norm) plus #12's 25-step late validation; the 3-space re-indentation inflates the raw diff vs #1. WD 0.025 also matches #6/#12.
edge.noise: 3-space re-indentation of the whole file, extra imports (math, random, numpy), per-trial seeding with num_trials=25, unused Muon class/muon_update and spectral_lam, commented-out old validation line.

techniques.note: NS polar (12 iters) of heavy-ball Nesterov momentum, max(1,m/n)^0.5; lr 0.02, wd 0.025
C·NS(X)·‖u‖_F^p, C = 2nd-order Taylor of (XXᵀ)^(p/2); p sigmoid +0.12 → −0.25
AdamW embed 0.3 / head 1/320 / 1-D 0.01, betas (0.8, 0.95), eps 1e-10, wd 0
flat for 30%, then linear to 0 at step 3200 (cooldown_frac 0.7)
train_steps 3200, claimed at the step-3175 eval
proj weights (attn/mlp/lm head) zero; others N(0, 0.33/fan_in); all biases 0

mechanisms.name: DynMuon (scheduled spectral power around the polar factor)
mechanisms.explain: dynmuon_update normalizes the summed gradient by 524288 tokens, forms heavy-ball Nesterov momentum u = 0.95m + g, and fast_spectral computes Y = NS(X) for X = u/‖u‖_F, then C·Y·‖u‖_F^p with C = I + δE + ½δ(δ−1)E², E = XXᵀ − I, δ = p/2 — a second-order Taylor surrogate for UΣ^pVᵀ that is exactly Muon at p = 0. Because XXᵀ has eigenvalues σᵢ²/Σσ² ≤ 1, C's eigenvalues stay in a narrow band (≈0.915–1 at p = +0.12, 1–1.195 at p = −0.25, weak directions getting the extreme value), while ‖u‖_F^p rescales the whole step with the momentum norm. p follows a decreasing sigmoid (asymptotes 0.25/−0.25, center and width 4% of 3200 steps): ≈+0.116 at step 0, 0 at step 128, ≈−0.24 by step 640.

caveats: The table's 'p: 0.25 → −0.25' are the sigmoid's asymptotes; the realized schedule starts at p≈+0.116 and reaches ≈−0.24 by step 640. The Taylor expansion is centered at XXᵀ = I, far from where it is evaluated (eigenvalues sum to 1), so the spectral reshaping is much weaker than an exact Σ^p — e.g. at p = −0.25 a direction with σ²/Σσ² = 1/768 gets ≤1.195× instead of 2.29× — and the uniform factors (≈1.2 and ‖u‖_F^−0.25) may matter as much as the reshaping. lam/spectral_lam is never used. No README.
